summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The scenario is Fig. 14a/14b of STREAM (W2898047526): a two-layer 3D IC with 32 Alpha 21264 cores and 144 TSVs, where transient maximum temperature is governed by closed-loop lifetime MPC with DVFS. The extraction labels it custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and no power_w, so Studio input validation failed (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). Because the experiment is a custom 2D steady run, it would have no transient trace even if it had run. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and it uses no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers. No source commit or generated-placement assumption applies, and no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was produced. The gate (deterministic, based on the feasibility verdict and Studio input validity) sets simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false, so no numeric comparison is made and nothing here claims replication. The paper's reported values are about 110 C free-run peak, a 90 C threshold with the existing method held below it, and a lifetime deposit exhausted at about 240 s. These are approximate text or figure readings of a transient chip-maximum under DVFS control, with 20 C ambient and a HotSpot 3D compact model, and no Studio-side value exists to compare against them. Qualitatively, the paper's result depends on workload phases, DVFS actuation, vertical inter-layer coupling and the lifetime-banking policy, none of which a steady single-layer thermal solve captures. Independent adversarial and page/asset reviews are also unresolved, so even the extracted evidence is not independently verified.

The paper models a two-layer 3D IC with TSVs, TSV-induced thermomechanical stress and inter-layer coupling. A Studio 2D single-layer model cannot represent the vertical stacking, TSV heat paths or stress.
The observable is a transient maximum temperature under a time-varying synthetic workload with DVFS feedback. A steady-state 2D model cannot reproduce it.

The result depends on closed-loop lifetime MPC with lifetime banking and DVFS actuation. This controller, with its ANN stress model, MTTF reliability models (thermal cycling and stress migration) and LTDP lifetime deposit, has no counterpart in a plain thermal solver.
The optimizer is a model predictive controller plus RPROP ANN training, not a floorplan or placement optimizer. The paper provides no placement coordinates for an optimization comparison.
The paper uses HotSpot 3D with a 92-node compact model, Wattch power traces, and COMSOL for stress. The solver, grid and package model differ from the Studio solver.
